title: Spell Sigils
summary: Animated magic circles for Pathfinder 2e spells, each derived from the spell's rank, traditions, traits and category.
tagline: An animated magic circle for every Pathfinder spell.
description: Pick any of more than 2,000 Pathfinder Second Edition spells, focus spells and rituals and watch its magic circle draw itself. Rank, traditions, traits and category decide the sigil's bands, geometry, colours and glyphs, and a random stream seeded on the spell's identity fills in the rest, so a spell always produces the same sigil, and each spell is different.

features.title: Drawn from the rules
features.description: Rank sets the rune bands and the sides of the central polygon, traditions set the colours and the runes, and traits appear as glyphs in medallions round the ring.

features.title: The same sigil every time
features.description: Each sigil comes from a random stream seeded on the spell's identity, so a spell draws the same circle on every visit and every device.

features.title: Ritual caster stations
features.description: A ritual is ringed by caster stations, the primary caster at the bottom, each marked with the sigil of a skill its checks accept and ruled to show the proficiency needed.

features.title: Focus spells
features.description: Focus spells take their class's colour and are written as spaced script with no ruled lines, as personal magic rather than tradition magic.

features.title: Search and filter
features.description: Search by name, filter by tradition, rank, ritual or focus spell, and narrow focus spells by class.

features.title: Parchment mode
features.description: Shows the sigil in ink on paper, each tradition in its own ink, with trait glyphs and skill sigils picked out in red as in a manuscript.

features.title: Max glow
features.description: Holds the sigil at the peak of the glow it flashes once when it finishes drawing.

features.title: Export
features.description: Copy, save or share the sigil as a PNG, with or without its background, or as an animation of it being drawn, in MP4 or WebM. In parchment mode it can also be saved as an SVG, which stays sharp at any size in a document or in print.

features.title: A link for every spell
features.description: The address names the spell on show, so a link opens the same sigil.

features.title: Symbol atlas
features.description: A separate page shows every rune, trait glyph and skill sigil the sigils are drawn from.

features.title: Help
features.description: A short guide to reading a sigil, with example spells to open.

features.title: Reduced motion
features.description: With the system set to reduce motion, each sigil fades in whole, without the drawing, the flash or the circling sparks.

features.title: Light and dark
features.description: The spell list follows the system's light or dark setting, while the sigil keeps its dark stage unless parchment is chosen.

features.title: Phones and tablets
features.description: The layout adapts to the screen, with the spell list in a drawer on a phone.

origin.title: From props to code
origin.body: I used to make scrolls as props for my players, and I wanted them to have a distinct visual element so that a scroll wasn't simply a page of words. Finding or making the images wasn't easy. Years later, after our move to digital, I still liked the art of casters surrounded by magic as they cast. I decided to see if I could create a magic circle in code, with enough parameters to vary it but rules to follow, so that every sigil shared common elements. Traits and traditions were the answer to that. The result is Spell Sigils. At first it was only the glowing version on screen, but given where the idea started, I wanted a way for people to make their own scroll art, and to share it.
